Honoured to be Featured in Defining Style: The Book of Interior Design by Phaidon

We are thrilled to share that our work has been published in Defining Style: The Book of Interior Design, the definitive new global survey of contemporary interior design by Phaidon.




Curated by the editors of Phaidon, this landmark book presents a richly illustrated and thoughtfully selected collection of 100 of the most innovative and inspiring interior design studios from around the world. To be featured among such a distinguished cohort of designers and visionaries is a true honour and a humbling milestone for our practice.




Our inclusion in Defining Style reflects not just a visual sensibility, but a deeper design philosophy—one that balances form and function, material honesty, and emotional resonance. The project selected for the book exemplifies our ongoing exploration of spatial storytelling, restraint, and atmosphere.




Phaidon’s global platform has long set the benchmark for excellence in art, design, and culture publishing. Being part of this beautifully crafted volume reinforces our commitment to timeless, thoughtful design and pushes us to continue creating work that speaks across disciplines and borders.

We extend our heartfelt thanks to the Phaidon editorial team for recognizing our work, and to our clients, collaborators, and craftsmen who help bring our vision to life.




We invite you to explore Defining Style: The Book of Interior Design, available here, and to discover a global snapshot of interior design today—one that is as diverse as it is inspiring.

✴ Vani Bhutani, the creative force behind it all, started her career as an interior designer in 2007.







✴  From humble beginnings with 6th Degree Associates in 2010 (alongside 2 others), to founding Vani Bhutani Designs in 2014, the vision has always been clear: creating spaces that inspire & resonate.







✴  Our work has been recognized time and again—published Multiple times in iconic magazines like Architectural Digest (AD), Elle Decor, & Indoor Outdoor Magazine. 







✴  With over 60 residential projects completed in Surat alone, and many more across the state, we’re proud to have shaped homes that tell unique stories.

Matcha Labs (2026)

✦

900 Sq. Ft.

Surat

In the bustling city of Surat, where urban culture is already thriving, a new, more contemplative experience begins to take shape. Conceived by Manan Butani—the mind behind the widely popular World of Desserts— Matcha Labs emerges as an intimate 900-square-foot café envisioned as a cultural bridge. The space is rooted in a clear and focused brief: to translate the essence of Japanese living into a serene, immersive environment. More than just a café, it is imagined as a calm, Zen-like retreat—an understated yet refined hub for the city’s growing community of matcha enthusiasts.







When we first visited the site, it was a long, rectangular space that felt quite closed and linear. From the outset, the idea was to shift this into something more layered and immersive, drawing from the quietness often found in Japanese spaces. Rooted in the quiet sensibility of Wabi-Sabi, the design of Matcha Labs embraces imperfection, restraint, and material authenticity. Instead of using obvious cultural elements, the space interprets Japanese design through atmosphere—calm, tactile, and introspective. The intention was to create a pause within the city, where simplicity and stillness become the defining experience, allowing visitors to engage more mindfully with both the space and the ritual of matcha. 







A carefully curated material palette anchors the space in subtle richness. Concrete walls finished in a soft ombré texture form a muted, almost meditative backdrop, shifting gently with light through the day. This is juxtaposed with raw, uncut rock detailing beneath the main display counter, reinforcing a sense of natural imperfection and groundedness. The entrance is marked by a charred timber door—its burnt finish adding depth, texture, and a tactile introduction to the space beyond.

Swipe ↔ 

At the heart of the café lies the live preparation counter, conceived as the primary visual and experiential anchor. This interactive element brings the craft of matcha-making into focus, transforming the act into a performance. Complementing this is a central rotating display unit that elevates the product itself—allowing it to be viewed from all angles, almost like a curated exhibit. Together, these elements ensure that the product remains at the core of the spatial narrative. 







 The interventions were subtle but intentional— softening the geometry, introducing variation in the ceiling, and allowing light to play a more active role. As the design evolved, elements like a sloped ceiling, soft wall washers, and suspended lighting were introduced to break the linearity of the space. Introducing natural elements was always part of the larger intent. It wasn’t about making them stand out, but about how they shape the space's experience over time. Plants and a subtle water body bring in a quiet sense of movement, something that shifts gently through the day without demanding attention. Gradually, these elements blend into the background, not as features but as part of the overall environment — leaving behind a space that feels composed, unhurried, and easy to be in.

E-SERVICES
 E-services 



✴ Online Interior Design Consultation (60–90 mins)




Deliverables:

* 60–90 minute Zoom/Google Meet session

* Follow-up summary email with discussed ideas

* Mood/inspiration board (optional)

* Basic sketch (if required)

* List of recommended improvements (lighting, layout, paint, furniture ideas)




一一一一一一一一一一一一一

✴ Virtual Room Design Package




Best For: Clients wanting a full redesign of a room without a site visit




Deliverables:

* 1-on-1 design brief meeting (30–45 mins)

* Mood board & concept board

* 2D room layout/floor plan (with furniture placements)

* 3D visualisation / photorealistic render (1–2 views)

* Shopping list with vendor links (India-based)

* 1 round of revisions

* Styling guide (PDF)




一一一一一一一一一一一一一

✴ Complete Home Design (up to 3BHK, remote)




Best For: NRIs, busy professionals, or clients doing remote build/renovation




Deliverables:

* Virtual consultation + site measurements (by client/local contractor)

* Concept presentation for each room

* Full space planning & furniture layout (AutoCAD or PDF)

* Material/fabric recommendations

* 3D renders (2 per room)

* Electrical, ceiling, lighting, and flooring layout (basic)

* Shopping list + style guide

* 2 revisions included

一一一一一一一一一一一一一

✴ Design & Decor Styling Boards




Best For: Clients needing aesthetic direction, not architectural work







Deliverables:

* Style survey form

* Theme/mood board

* Color palette

* Furniture + décor selection (images + links)

* Simple layout suggestion (optional)

* PDF guide to assemble the look




一一一一一一一一一一一一一

✴ Designer-on-Call Monthly Subscription




Best For: Ongoing clients who want regular design help




Deliverables:

* 4–6 virtual calls per month (15–30 mins each)

* Email/WhatsApp support

* Mini layout sketches or design suggestions

* Vendor/product recommendations

* Styling guidance

* Access to the designer's preferred vendor list




一一一一一一一一一一一一一

✴ Customised Furniture Design (Digital Service)




Best For: Clients looking to get furniture made locally using her design




Deliverables:

* Call to understand requirements

* 2D Sketch or 3D model

* Material suggestions (wood, finish, fabrics)

* Size and dimensions sheet

* Vendor notes or fabrication instructions

* 1 revision




一一一一一一一一一一一一一

✴ Interior Brand Collaborations / Product Styling




Best For: Home décor brands, product shoots, content styling




Deliverables:

* 3–5 mood boards

* Styling plan for the product

* Visual concepts for marketing/social

* Optional: Styling + feedback for shoots done remotely

* Brand usage guidelines




一一一一一一一一一一一一一

✴ Interior Review & Feedback Service




Best For: Clients who’ve done their interiors but want a pro’s opinion




Deliverables:

* Review of photos/videos/drawings

* Written report with improvement tips

* Suggestions for furniture rearrangement

* Lighting and styling feedback

* Optional: 1 virtual walkthrough.
